I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over fifty years. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil — it's the North China Plain, flat, good for wheat and maize. The well is reliable. Two of us now, just me and my wife. At seventy-one, I can't do as much as before, so I don't take risks or try new things I don't understand.

My 5 mu breaks down like this: 3 mu I rotate between winter wheat and summer maize — that's my main system, always has been. The other 2 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton pays better per mu but it wears me out at harvest. I'll keep it at 2 mu because I can still manage that. Any more and my back won't hold.

**Wheat (3 mu, planted October):** I'll use the same improved variety I've been buying from the village supply station — nothing fancy, but I know it germinates well in my soil. I'll spread base fertilizer before planting — diammonium phosphate and urea mixed in, then topdress with urea at jointing in April. Four irrigations: the pre-winter water in November, jointing, heading, and grain-filling. I always do four. Three pesticide sprays — herbicide in winter, then aphids and powdery mildew in spring. I'll rotary till after maize harvest in October to prepare the seedbed.

**Maize (3 mu, planted June after wheat harvest):** I buy hybrid seed — Zhengdan 958 mostly, everyone around here uses it and it yields well. I plant directly into the wheat stubble, no tilling. I'll apply fertilizer at planting and topdress at the big bell stage. Two extra irrigations if August is dry, otherwise the rain usually handles it. Two pesticide passes — herbicide early and one for pests if needed.

**Cotton (2 mu, planted April):** I've grown cotton my whole life. Hybrid seed again. Cotton needs a lot of care — six pesticide applications across the season for bollworm and aphids, you can't skip those. I'll irrigate four times, plough in spring to prepare. It's hard work in September-October picking, but it's worth it.
